published: directional ablation sharply lowers refusal on harmful prompts in 13 chat models (Arditi et al. Fig. 1)
ours: refusal on 64 harmful test prompts: 86% [75, 92] → 0% [0, 6] (random direction: 84% [74, 91]; Wilson 95% CIs)
criterion: ablation cuts refusal by ≥ 50 points while the random direction changes it by < 15

claim: Adding the direction makes the model refuse harmless requests
published: activation addition induces refusal on harmless instructions (§3)
ours: refusal on 64 harmless prompts: 6% [2, 15] → 98% [92, 100] (random direction: 6% [2, 15]; Wilson 95% CIs)
criterion: addition raises refusal by ≥ 50 points while the random direction raises it by < 15

claim: Control: a label-shuffled direction neither removes nor induces refusal
published: the refusal effect is specific to the harmful − harmless direction
ours: shuffled-label direction: harmful refusal 86% [75, 92] → 94% [85, 98] when ablated; harmless refusal 6% [2, 15] → 2% [0, 8] when added (Wilson 95% CIs)
post_hoc: stronger control added after the methods review
